source_basis: Lightfoot/Harmer1891 physical410–413 visually re-read. Continuous Greek throughS9xxx2; edited ancient Latin Vulgata fromxxx3, not Greek. Amherst190h primary edition and plate previously checked; its exact contribution is bounded below.

decisions.evidence: Working edition εὐειδέστεροι compared with L1/L2/E; reportedA ἀηδέστεροι.
full_English_alternatives: Why do all the trees bear fruit, but some of their fruits are more beautiful?
Why do all the trees bear fruit, but some of their fruits are more unpleasant?
decisions.rationale: The later superior-fruit explanation coheres with more beautiful. Keep the printed correction with an exposed Athos alternative; direct manuscript/version collation remains pending.

decisions.evidence: Damaged-word corner marks and apparatus attribute οὐκοῦν μακαρίζετε supply toGebhardt.
decisions.selected_English: So count yourselves blessed. Yet you think you have done a great deed if one of you suffers for God.
decisions.rationale: Read μακαρίζετε imperatively; preserve the contrast with life as the Lord’s gift. Editorial restoration does not become manuscript ink.

decisions.evidence: inventi conjectural with reportedL2 support versus citedL1 iuvenes. Amherst h does not certify this word.
full_English_alternatives: All these, however, were found white, both those who have believed and those who will believe.
All these, however, are white and young, those who have believed and those who will believe.
decisions.rationale: Follow the explicit printed correction with a footnote; do not claim Amherst confirms it.

decisions.evidence: Amherst h verso3–5 partly preserves same-kind/innocent-kind wording. Future-belief wording in1–2 remains partly supplied; not continuousGreek.
decisions.selected_English: For they are of the same kind. Blessed is this kind, because it is innocent.
decisions.rationale: This is the continuousLatin sense, supported in part by Greek. Do not infer complete Greek confirmation or use genus as a newly inserted ethnic classification.

decisions.evidence: †posse eos veritati favere† remains dagger-marked in continuousLatin. Printed apparatus proposes posse servitatem (or servitutem) agnoscere from version reports/Latin variants. Amherst h stopsbeforethisclause.
full_English_alternatives: When the Lord saw their disposition—that they could favor the truth and also remain good—he ordered their wealth to be cut back.
Editorial-conjecture alternative for the uncertain clause only: that they could recognize their servitude.
decisions.rationale: Keep the printed wording provisionally, flag the crux, and report rather than silently adopt the conjecture. No independent Greek support for this clause.

manuscript_limits: One Athos codex and one Amherst codex are not multiplied by printed editions or correcting hands. Latin/Palatina/Ethiopic apparatus reports are not fresh individual manuscript collations. Some Greek words are supplied in damaged Athos text. No independent reviewer or full collation claim.
